title: Government Strengthens Cyber Security Capacity of Women Officials through CyberShakti Programme
body_text:
The Government has taken note of the recommendation of the 2026 Standing Committee Report on the Empowerment of Women to scale up the CyberShakti programme. The programme was approved for a period of two years starting from October 2024 with the objective of enhancing cyber security awareness and strengthening cyber security skills among women government officials. The second phase of the project is recommended by the working group on Cyber Security in May 2026.
A total of 978 women government officials including women police officers, cyber cell personnel and women officials dealing with victims of cybercrimes have been trained under the CyberShakti programme since its inception in 2024 through 2-week Virtual Instructor-Led Training (VILT) mode online training programme and one-week offline residential training programme. The State/UT-wise details of women government officials trained under the CyberShakti programme since its inception in 2024:
S. No. State No. of Women Official Trained 1 Andhra Pradesh 12 2 Assam 11 3 Bihar 11 4 Chhattisgarh 6 5 Goa 7 6 Gujarat 81 7 Haryana 42 8 Himachal Pradesh 30 9 Jharkhand 11 10 Karnataka 73 11 Kerala 36 12 Madhya Pradesh 15 13 Maharashtra 53 14 Manipur 5 15 Meghalaya 16 16 Mizoram 2 17 Nagaland 1 18 Odisha 32 19 Punjab 12 20 Rajasthan 29 21 Sikkim 1 22 Tamil Nadu 64 23 Telangana 28 24 Tripura 19 25 Uttar Pradesh 45 26 Uttarakhand 32 27 West Bengal 20 Total 694
S. No. Union Territory (UT) No. of Women Official Trained 1 Andaman & Nicobar Islands 1 2 Chandigarh 7 3 Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu 2 4 Delhi 249 5 Jammu and Kashmir 5 6 Ladakh 12 7 Lakshadweep 1 8 Puducherry 7 Total 284
In addition to the training programmes, a total of 573 women participants have attended webinars aimed at sensitizing them toward the importance of cyber security.
This information was submitted by Union Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada in Rajya Sabha on 07.08.2026.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Electronics & IT informed the Rajya Sabha that 978 women government officials, including police officers and cyber cell personnel, have been trained under the CyberShakti programme since its launch in October 2024. The two-year programme uses two-week virtual instructor-led training and one-week offline residential training, with Delhi (249) and Gujarat (81) among the top contributors. The government has noted the 2026 Standing Committee's recommendation to scale up the programme, and a working group on Cyber Security recommended a second phase in May 2026.
enrichment.context:
CyberShakti reflects growing government focus on building institutional capacity to tackle cybercrime, particularly crimes against women, by equipping women officials—especially those in law enforcement and victim support roles—with technical skills to investigate and respond to cyber offences. This ties into broader digital governance initiatives such as the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Cyber Crime Prevention against Women and Children (CCPWC) scheme, and the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, all aimed at strengthening India's cyber security ecosystem amid rising internet penetration and digital crime.

The uneven state-wise distribution of trained officials (Delhi accounting for a large share, while several northeastern and smaller states have very few) highlights persistent regional disparities in capacity building, a recurring theme in governance and women's empowerment discussions. Parliamentary oversight, as seen through the Standing Committee on Empowerment of Women and the associated working group's recommendation for scaling up, exemplifies the legislative-executive feedback loop that shapes programme continuity and design in India's policy-making process.

prelims_questions.question: The 'CyberShakti' programme, discussed in Parliament in 2026, is associated with which of the following objectives?
options: Providing financial literacy training to rural women
Enhancing cyber security awareness and skills among women government officials
Setting up all-women cyber crime police stations across India
Providing digital identity cards to women entrepreneurs
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, CyberShakti aims to enhance cyber security awareness and strengthen cyber security skills among women government officials, including police officers and cyber cell personnel.

prelims_questions.question: Under which ministry does the CyberShakti programme fall?
options: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
prelims_questions.explanation: The release is issued by the Ministry of Electronics & IT, which administers the CyberShakti programme.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of capacity-building programmes like CyberShakti in strengthening India's response to cybercrimes against women. What structural challenges hinder uniform implementation across states and UTs?

Cybercrime poses an evolving challenge to internal security and gender safety in India. Examine the institutional and policy measures taken by the government to build technical capacity among law enforcement personnel to counter this threat.
